question: What represents the starting point in the chain of infection?
explanation: The source of infection acts as the origin where the infectious agent lives and multiplies before moving to a new host. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why must every link in the chain of infection remain intact?

options.A: To allow the disease to transmit successfully
options.B: To prevent the immune system from responding
options.C: To speed up the incubation period of bacteria
options.D: To guarantee complete recovery of the patient

explanation: If any single link in the chain is broken, the infectious agent cannot reach or infect a new host. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the natural home where a germ normally lives and multiplies called?
explanation: A reservoir is the natural habitat where an organism survives and multiplies over time. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h2)

question: How does a source of infection differ from a reservoir?

options.A: The reservoir is always an inanimate object while the source is living
options.B: The source is the immediate point from which the germ transfers to a host
options.C: The reservoir is the final destination of the infectious agent
options.D: The source only harbors viruses while the reservoir harbors bacteria

explanation: The source is where the infection is directly caught, whereas the reservoir is the broader, long-term home for the germ. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h2)

question: Which human source harbors a pathogen without ever showing signs of illness?
explanation: Healthy carriers shed infectious agents into the environment without experiencing any clinical symptoms themselves. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h3)

question: What makes convalescent carriers a major challenge in infection control?

options.A: They refuse to isolate because they feel physically strong
options.B: They display more severe symptoms than primary clinical cases
options.C: They are completely immune to standard antibiotic treatments
options.D: They continue shedding germs even after recovering from symptoms

explanation: Convalescent carriers look and feel healthy, leading others to let down their guard while they still spread microbes. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h3)

question: What term describes infections that spread naturally from animals to humans?
explanation: Zoonoses are infections shared between animals and human populations under natural conditions. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h4)

question: A cholera outbreak linked to a flooded community stream demonstrates which type of source?
explanation: Contaminated water supplies and soil represent environmental reservoirs and sources of waterborne germs. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the first case identified in a disease outbreak called?
explanation: The index case is the first patient brought to the attention of epidemiologists during an investigation. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why is tracing the source of an infection critical during a hospital ward outbreak?

options.A: To assign legal blame to specific staff members
options.B: To determine the financial cost of patient care
options.C: To eliminate the need for routine hand hygiene
options.D: To stop further transmission by isolating the origin

explanation: Finding the source allows nurses and infection control teams to implement targeted barriers and stop the spread. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which nursing action directly neutralizes a human source of bacterial infection?
explanation: Effective antimicrobial therapy kills the pathogen within the human source, stopping active shedding. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why is isolating an infectious patient considered a primary source-control measure?

options.A: It boosts the immune system of healthcare workers
options.B: It disinfects the air inside the hospital room
options.C: It cures the patient of the underlying disease faster
options.D: It physically separates the source from susceptible hosts

explanation: Isolation stops the pathogen from bridging the gap between the infected source and uninfected individuals. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h6)
